title: Linear threshold approximation by juntas
statement: Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be a linear threshold function, and let $0<\epsilon,\eta<1/2$. There exist a set $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and a Boolean function $g$ depending on at most $|J|$ coordinates such that $|J|\le 1+\dfrac{I(f)^{2+\eta}}{\epsilon^{1+\eta}}\left(\dfrac{2}{\eta}+1\right)^{2\lceil16/\epsilon^2\rceil}$ and the fraction of inputs on which $f$ and $g$ differ is at most $\epsilon$, where $I(f)$ is the total influence of $f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
